seo_title: KARL STORZ Case Study: Meta Lead Click-Through | SOMIN
description: With SOMIN, KARL STORZ moved APAC Meta ads for 11 markets into accounts it owns, and link click-through on lead campaigns rose 33%, from 0.69% to 0.91%.
eyebrow: Brand case study · Medical technology · Asia Pacific
h1: KARL STORZ owns its APAC Meta ads, and lead click-through rose 33%
lede: KARL STORZ moved its Asia Pacific Meta advertising into accounts it owns. With SOMIN, its regional team runs paid social for 11 markets and plans creative with competitor and audience data. Link click-through on lead campaigns rose by a third, from 0.69% to 0.91%.
meta_line: A SOMIN results case study · Facebook and Instagram lead campaigns · 20 Apr to 4 Nov, 2025 against 2026

challenge.title: Why KARL STORZ wanted to own its paid social
challenge.body: KARL STORZ reaches clinicians in 11 Asia Pacific markets, with small budgets per market and strict rules on medical-device advertising. In 2025 its Meta ad account and pixel sat with its agency, and its own team had partial access. The brief asked for ownership of the account and pixel, competitor and audience insight to act on, and support for strategy and creative.

approach.title: Five steps SOMIN and KARL STORZ took across 11 markets
points: Moved campaigns to owned accounts, so the team sees every campaign's data directly.
Tested AI audiences beside specialty audiences in the same campaigns, comparable by market and week.
Built competitor analysis into planning: one dashboard tracks rivals' posts and paid ads by market and specialty.
Found open ground in gynaecology, where no brand published diagnostic education, and built a new campaign on that gap.
Used SOMIN personas and concepts as starting points, finished with real product imagery, brand elements and regulatory review.

findings_title: KARL STORZ click-through by lead offer, 2025 against 2026

findings.title: Content offers rose 55%
findings.body: Guides, eBooks and webinars went from 0.63% to 0.99% link click-through on Facebook and Instagram.

findings.title: Event and course sign-ups rose 22%
findings.body: Courses, congresses and services went from 0.72% to 0.87% link click-through.

findings.title: The rise holds country by country
findings.body: All lead campaigns went from 0.69% to 0.91%, a range of +18% to +50%, and the changes hold when each country is compared only with itself.

delivered.title: What changed in KARL STORZ's creative and planning
points: Video grew from 7% to 34% of ad spend, from Meta Ads Manager, 28 Aug to 4 Nov in both years
Creative diversity rose from 71 to 78 on SOMIN's Meta Diversity score, 39 creatives in each period
One dashboard of competitors' public posts and ads, where every insight opens the original ad or post
New creative across the region every 15 days, briefed from competitor activity and audience research

quote.text: SOMIN helps the creative team to ideate newer campaign assets that they haven't considered.
quote.source: Digital Marketing Manager, South East Asia and Taiwan, KARL STORZ

outcome.title: A like-for-like before and after for KARL STORZ
outcome.body: Click-through rose for content offers and for event sign-ups once KARL STORZ ran its own accounts. The two periods ran in different accounts with different campaigns, so this is a before and after, not a controlled test.

faq.a: Link click-through: clicks to the landing page divided by impressions. Meta's "CTR (all)" also counts likes and expands, so it reads higher. Changes are calculated from unrounded rates.

faq.q: Why is Audience Network left out?
faq.a: Meta's automatic placements moved about 29% of 2026 lead spend there, against under 1% in 2025, and its clicks rarely reach the page.
Lead campaigns on Facebook and Instagram from 20 April to 4 November 2025, in the agency account, against the same dates in 2026, in the KARL STORZ account. Campaigns are grouped by their offer.

faq.q: What does the 15-day creative cycle involve?
faq.a: Read competitor activity in the market, find the open angle and the audience to target, draft concepts from personas and whitespace, build and review the ads with real assets, then launch in the owned account and report back.

faq.q: Where does the competitor data come from?
faq.a: From public posts and ads that SOMIN collects. The dashboard covers tactics, communication and activities, from offers and channels to launches and the latest competitor moves.
